messages.subject_clean: Problems building the Rmpfr package on the shinyapps.io sever
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

Recently I wanted to use the HH package for a shiny-markdown document. When I tried to deploy this document to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, I encountered a problem that the HH package could not be built on the server. After some testing, I found out that the Rmpfr depency is the real problem. Here a minimal example (test.Rmd)
----
title: "Untitled"
runtime: shiny
output: html_document
---

```{r}
require( Rmpfr )
```
The document works just well locally on my windows 7 machine. However, trying to upload it using shinyapps::deployapp() leads to the following error

configure: error: Header file mpfr.h not found; maybe use --with-mpfr-include=INCLUDE_PATH
ERROR: configuration failed for package ‘Rmpfr’
* removing ‘/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/Rmpfr’
################################# End Task Log #################################
Error: Unhandled Exception: Child Task 61322212 failed: Error building image: Error building Rmpfr (0.5-7). Build exited with non-zero status: 1
The full error log can be found in http://pastebin.com/D5KVc44n. About one year ago, I already had a document with a similar setup (using the HH package) on KDE 14.04 and the deployment worked fine. Any suggestions are welcome.

Beyond the HTTP timeout errors (which is solved if I attempt to deploy again), I found the reason to the different values. In my app, I use ddply in library(plyr) to do the following:

ddply(df_subset, c(x,"Question"), summarize, perc_yes=length(which(value == "YES"))/length(value),
                             perc_yes_label=paste0(" ",round(length(which(value == "YES"))/length(value)*100),"d))

          # when "YES" in local shiny is deployed, shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> shows "NO" values

library(ggvis)

    lb$input()  %>%

  flex.data %>%
    ggvis(~x.data, ~y.data) %>%
    layer_points() %>%
    layer_lines() %>%
    bind_shiny("ggvis_profile_plot")
})

messages.body_plain:
Originally I raised this as an issue at https://github.com/mtennekes/treemap/issues/23 but the problem seems to be related to how deployApp() installs packages.  An app using the {treemap} package will deploy ok if the client system has CRAN's version of {treemap}, but not if it has GitHub's.  In the snippet below, the 01_hello app has been modified just by adding the line
library(treemap)

library(shiny)
library(shinyapps)
library(devtools)

install.packages("treemap") # ie from cran

messages.body_plain:
Hi Mark,
Our retention policy is likely to change when we introduce persistent storage but as of today the storage on the instance you are running with will be around for as long as that application instance is up.  Recall that you can have multiple instances for a given application and so the storage is tied to the application instance today.
My recommendation for folks who care about making sure that their content is truly transient, is to write the files that are uploaded to /tmp.   That /tmp directory will be clean every time the application instance gets restarted for whatever reason.  Alternatively, you could register a handler on the session in the onSessionEnded to handle any cleanup you want to do.  Here is the link <http://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/latest/session.html> to the documentation for that.

Hope this helps.
-Tareef
